meta.title: Balaji Srinivasan - The Open Source Network State - TOKEN2049 Singapore 2026
meta.thread_line: 5 threads · cities as the new asset class · cloud-first startup societies · distressed real estate · society as a service and man-months · collective exit

snapshot: Balaji's thesis: after cryptocurrencies, the next crypto frontier is **crypto communities** — physical societies printed out of online ones.
Network School (2024, Malaysia island) drew thousands from 80+ countries, then moved to Kazakhstan on a better state offer.
A city is an asset: New York at ~$300-400K of real estate per person is a ~$2-3 trillion valuation, on par with the biggest companies.
Playbook of 12 concepts being open-sourced: cloud-first/land-last, pop-ups, distressed real estate, one commandment, society as a service.
Proposed metric for physical societies: **man-months** (people x months stayed), the analogue of market cap.
Defense model: the non-violent alternative to a military is mobility; collective exit, with offers from 10 countries.
A "crypto equity" for communities is teased as the way to pull future value into the present.

themes.title: Cities, not just companies and currencies, are the new competitive unit
themes.lead: The ultimate real-world asset is a community, a city, even a country.
bullets: Network State (book, 2022) asked whether giant social networks and crypto are the end of the road, or can be printed out physically.
Valuing New York: ~8.5M people x $300-400K real estate per person gives roughly $2-3 trillion; the largest companies, liquidated and rebuilt in one place, land at a similar scale.
Implications: a possible city asset (an "NYC or SF" token), and valuing China by Shanghai and Shenzhen as well as its tech companies.
Astana overtook San Francisco 10 years ago on growth and builds ~100x the housing; Kazakhstan is also building Alau Town, billed as the first crypto city.
A city need not sit in one place: Hilton's ~1 million beds, offices and restaurants worldwide are a "network city".

quote.text: The ultimate real-world asset is a community, a city, even a country.

themes.watch: Speaker runs Network School and is promoting the Network State conference; the valuation is his own rough estimate ("you can argue with it").

themes.title: Network School proved a community can be printed out, then moved
themes.lead: Bring thousands of people to one place, then relocate them as liquidly as in the digital world, with some friction.
bullets: Opened 2024 in a Malaysian ghost city on an island off Singapore; people from 80+ countries attended.
Malaysia stopped wanting them; Kazakhstan offered "an amazing deal" with full state support and attendance records followed.
Also moved the community to Próspera, and says offers came from 10 countries; the transcript also mentions a Costa Rica move and a Republic of Costa deal.
Analogy: when China shut down Bitcoin mining, Bitcoin redistributed to other nodes — the same robustness, now physical.
Peers named: Vitalik's Zuzalu and Bryan Johnson's Don't Die community, as networks of pop-ups that become permanent.
themes.watch: Destination details are inconsistent in the captions (Kazakhstan, Próspera, Costa Rica); all are reported as the speaker said them.

themes.title: The build playbook: cloud-first, pop-ups, distressed real estate
themes.lead: Start online, prove demand with pop-ups, then lease or buy already-built, under-used real estate.
bullets: **Cloud-first, land-last**: begin as a Substack or Telegram group motivated by something more than money.
**Pop-ups are the new startups**: print the cloud out for a limited time (Cursed Cafe, AngelList cafe, Coinbase taking over a small town), then build a waitlist for a permanent site.
Capital online, build offline — like Elon de-risking Tesla with an online waitlist; crowd-fund the community in crypto.
**Distressed real estate**: buy abandoned or de-industrialized towns; Japan has ~9 million empty homes; Magdalene College is 129 acres for sale.
**Frontier, not fancy**: recruit people who build like Habitat for Humanity, not guests of a resort; the East has seen cities built from nothing (a Chinese city shown 1984 vs 2023), the West less so.

themes.title: Designing the society: circles, one commandment, subscription, man-months
themes.lead: A startup society needs a reason to exist, tiered commitment, a business model and its own scoreboard.
bullets: **Concentric circles**: core team (core devs), long-termers (maximalists), members (holders), visitors — a continuum of engagement.
**One commandment**: select for a purpose beyond airdrops — vegan, language immersion, longevity, internet off at 9pm, carb-free; selective admission is legitimate like a college's.
**Society as a service**: the Google campus as a subscription (food, room, gym, events); bulk buying makes it "crypto Costco", a DAO in the physical world.
**Identity = community = security = territory**: token-gated digital access should match the physical checkpoint; some spaces must be members-only.
**Upside offsets utility**: like early Bitcoin or WhatsApp, a tiny network runs on upside; a "crypto equity" for communities is teased.
**Man-months** = people x months stayed, the physical analogue of coins x price; generalizes the census for nomads and is hard to fake with proof of human and proof of location.

quote.text: The non-violent alternative to a military is mobility.

themes.title: Collective exit replaces the military
themes.lead: A mobile tribe of tech people can bargain with states by threatening to sign with someone else.
bullets: Answer to "nation-states have militaries": Google and Bitcoin reached trillions without firing a shot.
Organized, premeditated flight beats a pointless fight; the Puritans' collective exit built the US.
Network School had offers from 10 countries and took the best; he says this leverage was theoretical a year ago and is now proven.
Frames it as unbundling the sovereign individual and rebundling a sovereign collective.
themes.watch: Critics' objection (no military, states will crush it) is answered by the speaker's own experience only.

takeaways.title: Think of communities and cities as the next asset class beyond coins and tokens.
Test any startup-society idea with an online group, then a pop-up, before touching real estate.
Target distressed, already-built property rather than empty land.
Score a physical community by man-months, not headcount.
Treat mobility and competing state offers as the bargaining lever.

hot_takes.take: The non-violent alternative to a military is mobility.
The network state is actually about distressed real estate.

claims.claim: New York City's real estate is worth about $2-3 trillion at $300-400K per person
claims.condition: assuming $300-400K of real estate per person

claims.claim: Network State conference is held at Marina Bay Sands, Singapore, with more detail on community equity

other_news.title: Sources referenced: his book The Network State (2022), Vitalik's Zuzalu, Bryan Johnson's Don't Die; conference at nsrconference.com.

glossary.def: A community that starts online, coordinates around a shared purpose, then crowd-funds and occupies physical territory.
Number of people times the months each stays in a society, proposed as the physical-world equivalent of market cap.
A subscription providing housing, food, gym and events, like a company campus.
A community relocating together to a more favorable jurisdiction instead of fighting.
